subject: Evidence staging & signoff roadmap for Private Deployment — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@orchidtx.com>, procurement@orchidtx.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Evidence staging & signoff roadmap for Private Deployment — next steps

Jordan — thanks again for the redlines on the MSA and the Order Form. I reviewed the highlights with the team this morning and wanted to propose a concrete roadmap so we can keep procurement moving without blocking your legal review.

High-level ask from Orchid: clarify operator access/kit handoff, snapshot custody, and a minimal set of artifacts that prove runbook execution capability. We've attached a draft evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.xlsx) and an annotated MSA showing where we think exhibits should live.

Proposed sequencing (short):
- Day 0–2: Redwood and Orchid agree on which exhibits are in-scope for the Order Form (operator runbook, snapshot procedure, witness protocol).
- Day 3–7: Redwood provides SOC2 summary + sample runbook snippets and a one-page operator checklist.
- Day 8–14: Orchid performs a short witness session (remote) or accepts a notarized snapshot hash; signoff captured via DocuSign.

Questions for you now:
1) Would Orchid accept a signed hash + S3/transfer bundle as a primary evidence method, or do you require a remote witness session for the first go-live?
2) Any procurement timelines we should target to avoid changing the go-live window?

Next steps: if you confirm the preferred evidence delivery (hash vs. live witness), I’ll loop in Ben (contracts) and Marissa (legal) to draft the exhibit language we’ll append to the Order Form. Happy to run a 30-min sync tomorrow.

Thanks —
Sean

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@orchidtx.com>

Date: 2028-07-14T12:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence staging & signoff roadmap for Private Deployment — next steps

Sean — appreciate the clear sequencing. Quick answers and our update: we prefer the signed-hash + transfer bundle approach for the initial acceptance if the signed-hash is accompanied by a short, timed witness call for chain-of-custody confirmation. That gives our security folks the forensic artifact they need without requiring an on-site witness for day-0.

A few clarifying redlines from our side (high level):
- License residency: we want explicit language limiting the licensed runtime to our VPC region and a technical annex that prevents unintentional snapshot export.
- Snapshot transfer: we will accept an S3 bundle over a pre-authorized account, but the transfer must be recorded and a signed SHA256 hash provided.
- Operator access: define an operator runbook exhibit with scope (read-only vs. exec) plus an operator account revocation SLA.

Procurement timeline: procurement needs an internal review window of 10 business days after the exhibits are finalized. That said, legal has some targeted edits they’ll send by end-of-day.

I’ll share our annotated redlines (PDF) in a follow-up. Can we lock a witness-slot for next Tue morning PST?

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
Director, IT & Security — Orchid Therapeutics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-07-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence staging & signoff roadmap for Private Deployment — next steps

Jordan / Sean — looping legal & contracts into the thread. Thanks for the preferences, Jordan. A few points from Redwood legal (we’ll keep this practical):

1) Exhibits and orderform language: we can add an "Operational Evidence Exhibit" to the Order Form that enumerates the deliverables (runbook snippets, signed-hash proof, transfer logs). We will propose sample language that: (a) limits Redwood's rights to the artifacts specifically listed; (b) states the snapshot transfer is strictly for validation and will not expand license scope; (c) allows Orchid to require immutable audit logs for the transfer window.

2) License residency and export protections: we will draft a narrow annex restricting model residency/use to Orchid’s authorized VPC endpoints and adding a prohibition on model export except as required for mutually agreed forensic purposes. That annex will include a brief definition of "export" to avoid ambiguity.

3) Witnessing & escrow-lite: we can offer an "escrow-lite" workflow — signed hashes + certified witness call, with a notarized digest if Orchid requests additional assurance. A full third-party code escrow would be a separate engagement; this exhibit is scoped only to operational handoff artifacts.

4) Evidence artifacts we need from Orchid to complete the exhibit:
- Target VPC CIDR(s) and S3 bucket account for transfer
- Primary procurement contact and legal reviewer (name + email)
- Confirmation if notarized digest is required or if DocuSign capture is sufficient
- Any internal compliance template Orchid requires us to fill (e.g., internal audit checklist)

Timeline suggestion: Ben and I will draft the exhibit language and the annotated Order Form by Fri EOD (2028-07-18). If Orchid Procurement confirms the 10-business-day review window, we can aim to complete mutual signoff by Aug 1.

We’ll attach the draft exhibit and the evidence checklist once they’re ready. Sean — let’s keep the witness-slot tentative for Tue morning PST; I’ll join as well.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment placeholders: sample_operator_runbook.txt (snippet), escrow-lite-term-sheet.pdf
